title: Genetic Basis of Diseases
objectives: Analyze disease-causing genetic variations at molecular level
Correlate mutation types with clinical phenotypes
Evaluate inheritance patterns in disease pedigrees
Apply genomic medicine approaches to diagnosis

inheritance_patterns.title: Disease Transmission
inheritance_patterns.content:
Imprinting Disorders
• Prader-Willi: Paternal 15q11-13 deletion
• Angelman: Maternal UBE3A mutation
• Testing: Methylation analysis
Mitochondrial
• Maternal inheritance
• Heteroplasmy threshold effect
• Examples: MELAS, LHON

genomic_medicine.title: Diagnostic Technologies
genomic_medicine.content:
Whole Exome Sequencing

Yield: 25-40% for neurodevelopmental disorders

Limitations: Non-coding variants, CNVs

Case: DYNC1H1 mutation in spinal muscular atrophy

Pharmacogenomics

TPMT: Thiopurine metabolism (3% poor metabolizers)

CYP2D6: Codeine activation (UMs vs PMs)

therapeutic_approaches.title: Genetic Therapies
therapeutic_approaches.content:
• Enzyme replacement: GAA for Pompe disease
  • Gene addition: AAV9-SMN1 for SMA
  • Gene editing: CRISPR for β-thalassemia trials
  • RNA therapy: Nusinersen splicing modifier

case_studies.title: Clinical Correlations
case_studies.content:
Familial Hypercholesterolemia

Gene: LDLR (1p32)

Mechanism: Impaired LDL clearance

Treatment: PCSK9 inhibitors + statins

Long QT Syndrome

Genes: KCNQ1/KCNH2/SCN5A

ECG: QTc >500ms risk for TdP

Therapy: β-blockers, ICD for type 1

faqs.title: FAQs
faqs.content:
Why do some autosomal dominant disorders have reduced penetrance?

Due to modifier genes (e.g., hypertrophic cardiomyopathy) or environmental factors (diet in hereditary hemochromatosis).

How can mitochondrial diseases show variable tissue involvement?

Heteroplasmy levels differ across tissues - high-energy organs (brain, muscle) exceed threshold first.

Why are trinucleotide repeat disorders anticipation diseases?

Meiotic instability causes expansion in successive generations (e.g., CAG repeats in Huntington's).
